title: ActionBar
description:
The `ActionBar` is the navigation bar located at the top of a page. Action items can be added to the action bar to execute actions relevant to the page context.
A back navigation button is automatically added to the `ActionBar` during navigation.
If too many items populate the `ActionBar`, an overflow button automatically appears in the top right corner, displaying excess items as a popover menu. The maximum number of visible items depends on the device type (tablet or phone) and the item type (text or icon). On a tablet, the maximum number of visible items, including the overflow button, is 4 for icons only and 3 if a text item is present. On a mobile phone, the maximum number of visible items, including the overflow button, is 3 for icons only and 2 if a text item is present.

The `ActionBar` can support styling at two different levels:

Application-level styling: This is done by defining a type selector CSS with the predefined type names `ActionBar` (using the color property to style the color of the caption, subhead, text items, and icon tint, and the background-color property to style the background color of the `ActionBar`; on Android, the same background color is applied to the status bar as well.  Not applicable for iOS 26 and above with Liquid Glass enabled.) and `ActionBarTitle` (to style the caption, large caption, and subhead).

Page-level styling: This is done by defining a CSS class name (class selector) for a subview or property in `ActionBar.Styles` or `ActionBar.Items.Style`.

Caption.description: Main caption / title of the page.

Subhead.description: Sub caption / sub title of the page. When `Subhead` is set, the `PrefersLargeCaption` property is ignored.

CaptionAlignment.description: Android only. Choose one of the options based on how you want to align the `Caption` and `Subhead`.

PrefersLargeCaption.description:
[Deprecated. Use `PreferredCaptionSize` instead.] iOS and Android only. Set as true to display in large caption mode. This property is ignored if `Subhead` is defined.

Specifically for iOS, this property is not supported on page with BottomNavigation, Tabs, SideDrawer, FormCellContainer, or FlexibleColumn as the control.

PreferredCaptionSize.description: iOS and Android only. Choose one of options based on your preferred size of the action bar.

enum.description: Display in large caption mode. When set, the `Subhead` property will be ignored.
Android only. Display in medium caption mode.

Logo.description: The icon can only be displayed on page without back navigation. The icon to be provided as app logo is displayed at the left most item on ActionBar. On iOS, The logo is displayed after `SideDrawer` menu button if app is using `SideDrawer`, the maximum size allowed is 24dp height x 48dp width. On Android, Logo can only be displayed if there is no SideDrawer and no back navigation button, maximum size allowed is 24dp height x 48dp width.

OverflowIcon.description: iOS only. The icon is to replace the overflow button icon (default ellipsis).

OnBackButtonPressed.description: This event is triggered when a user presses the back button in the action bar. This event will not be triggered when ClosePage action is triggered or System Back button (Android) is pressed. If a false is returned from the handler then the back navigation is cancelled, if true or void or undefined or null is returned then the back navigation continued.

DataSubscriptions.description: Array of data change events to subscribe to.

Styles.description: iOS and Android only. Set styles for actionbar.

ActionBar.description: The string value is a style class name of `ActionBar`. It is used to set the background color of the actionbar. Not applicable for iOS 26 and above with Liquid Glass enabled.

Caption.description: The string value is a style class name of `Caption`. It is used to style the `Caption` text on the actionbar.

Subhead.description: The string value is a style class name of `Subhead`. It is used to style the `Subhead` text on the actionbar.

Logo.description: The string value is a style class name of `Logo`.

OverflowIcon.description: iOS only. The string value is a style class name of `OverflowIcon`.

Items.description:
Each item represents a button displayed in the navigation bar.
For mobile, by default, all items are positioned to the right side of `ActionBar`.
When visible items exceed the max items allowed, an overflow button would automatically be displayed, excess items can be accessed through popover displayed when the overflow button is pressed.
The max items allowed vary based on several factors.
On tablet, icon only items has a maximum of 4 items, while text only items or mixed items have a maximum of 3 items.
On phone, icon only items has a maximum of 3 items, while text only items or mixed items have a maximum of 2 items.
